thread:
maya: heads up — the new HF spm model we tried to bring up shows weird chat breaks after conversion to BPE. short thread with repro and questions.

liam: can you paste the exact symptom? is it tokenization mismatch or model output quality?

maya: token mismatch first. chat templates that rely on <|system|> and <|user|> get glued together. prompts that used to be 4 tokens now become 1 or 0 in some cases. example: 'System:\n' -> becomes empty prefix sometimes.

sasha: that sounds like special token id remapping gone wrong during spm->bpe conversion. did you use the HF tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids mapping after converting vocab/merges?

maya: we ran the conversion script (sentencepiece -> merges + vocab) from our onboarding gist but I noticed two things in the converted tokenizer.json:
- there are duplicated entries for "<|system|>" (one with id 5 and one with 1024)
- config.json had bos_token_id: 1 but model's embedding matrix seems aligned to a different ordering

chris: duplicated special tokens is classic SPM edge-case. SentencePiece can emit multiple byte sequences that normalize to the same string after whitespace stripping. conversion scripts that naively append special tokens to the vocab can create duplicates.

devon: quick check: run `tokenizer.unique_no_normalize = True`? actually HF Tokenizers has `add_special_tokens` behaviour — but easier: dump token -> id map and check for collisions.

maya: dump attached:``` 
# snippet
for t,i in tokenizer.get_vocab().items():
    if t.startswith("<|"):
        print(t,i)
```
output showed:```
<|pad|> 0
<|user|> 1
<|assistant|> 2
<|system|> 5
<|system|> 1024
```

liam: yep. That duplication is the root cause. When we save tokenizer.pretrained it keeps one of them in special_tokens_map and the other as a regular entry, so downstream code that uses special token ids (chat template formatter) picks the wrong id.

sasha: how did you generate merges? did you use byte-level BPE merges with a separate normalization step? If merges were created from normalized pieces but vocab kept raw SPM outputs, indices shift.

maya: we used sentencepiece export + a script to infer merges by pair counts. I think normalizer inconsistency happened: we applied `unicode_normalizer='nfkc'` in the BPE tokenizer but the original SPM model was no-normalization.

chris: plan: 1) canonicalize tokens by the same normalizer as SPM before building merges; 2) de-duplicate special tokens by string with preference to lowest id; 3) update config.json to match final special token ids; 4) run a token-id remapping step that updates model embedding rows to match new token ordering.

devon: for the remapping, this quick script worked for us last week:``` 
# remap embedding rows to new ids
old_vocab = old_tokenizer.get_vocab()
new_vocab = new_tokenizer.get_vocab()
new_emb = torch.zeros_like(old_model.transformer.wte.weight)
for tok, new_id in new_vocab.items():
    old_id = old_vocab.get(tok)
    if old_id is None:
        new_emb[new_id] = torch.randn(old_model.config.hidden_size) * 0.02  # random init
    else:
        new_emb[new_id] = old_model.transformer.wte.weight[old_id]
old_model.transformer.wte.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(new_emb)
torch.save(old_model.state_dict(), "remapped_model.bin")
```

maya: thanks — we'll try that. two follow-ups: (a) any pros/cons for choosing to prefer low-id special token vs high-id? (b) will quantized variants get broken if ids shift?

sasha: (a) prefer whichever id was referenced in model weights originally — that's typically the lower id but not guaranteed. Use embedding-content match heuristic: compare embedding vectors for each duplicate token string and pick the id whose embedding is non-zero/meaningful. (b) quantized variants: yes, if you change token ordering you must remap the embedding table before quantizing or re-quantize after remap. Old quantized checkpoint will be misaligned otherwise.

liam: small QA: check chat template code — we should assert `special_tokens_map` ids exist in tokenizer.get_vocab() and that model.config.{bos_token_id,eos_token_id,pad_token_id} match those values at load-time and warn on mismatch.

maya: filed a tiny PR in onboarding repo with detection + remediation script. Will run onboarding harness (sanity prompts + dev evals) after remap.

evals-bot: perf delta for v0 -> remapped v1: latency +3% (embedding rebuild), end-to-end pass rate on chat template sanity tests improved from 82% -> 99%

chris: nice. one more gotcha: some HF chat templates embed token ids directly in template strings (we do this in a few legacy evals). search for occurrences of "<\|system\|>" literal vs tokenizer.special_tokens_map usage.

maya: good catch — found 3 legacy tests. updating them to call tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids at runtime.

devon: if anyone's converting more SPM models: share that normalizer + dedupe checklist. saved us a day. :party_parrot: 

liam: can you paste the PR link when ready? will review.

maya: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/248 — includes repro, remap script, and updated config validator.

sasha: great thread. small note: add a unit test that simulates duplicate special tokens (two strings mapping to same normalized text) to prevent regressions.

maya: done — thanks all.
